failures.title: Alfa Romeo 955A3000 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: EGR valve clogging
items.whatHappens: The 955A3000 is prone to EGR valve clogging due to soot buildup from the exhaust gas recirculation system. Symptoms include rough idle, hesitation, loss of power, increased fuel consumption, and the check engine light illuminating.
items.repairVsReplace: EGR valve cleaning (around £200-£400) is usually sufficient; if the valve is damaged, replacement costs around £400-£700. This is a maintenance issue, not a reason for engine replacement. Read our full EGR valve failure guide

items.title: DPF (Diesel Particulate Filter) blockage
items.whatHappens: The DPF can become blocked, particularly on vehicles used predominantly for short urban journeys where the filter never reaches regeneration temperature. Symptoms include DPF warning light, reduced power, increased fuel consumption, and limp mode.
items.repairVsReplace: DPF cleaning (around £300-£600) is usually the first step; if the DPF is damaged, replacement costs £700-£1,200. Regular motorway driving helps prevent DPF issues.

items.title: Turbocharger wear
items.whatHappens: The turbocharger on the 955A3000 can experience wear at higher mileages, particularly if oil changes have been neglected or if the EGR/DPF issues have caused excessive back pressure.
items.repairVsReplace: Turbocharger replacement (around £600-£1,200) is the standard fix. Regular oil changes with the correct specification are essential for turbo longevity.

items.title: Injector wear
items.whatHappens: The common‑rail injectors can wear over time, particularly with poor‑quality fuel. Symptoms include rough idle, excessive smoke, poor starting, and increased fuel consumption.
items.repairVsReplace: Injectors can be refurbished (around £150-£250 each) or replaced (around £300-£450 each).

failures.goodYearsLine: The 955A3000 is generally reliable when properly maintained. The 1.6 Multijet II is one of Fiat's most durable diesel platforms, with many examples exceeding 150,000 miles. Regular motorway driving for DPF regeneration and correct oil specification are the key factors for longevity.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the 955A3000
variants.intro: The 955A3000 is a specific engine code within the Fiat Multijet II family of diesel engines. Unlike some families that fragment into many sub‑codes, the 955A3000 variants are primarily distinguished by power output and application. Multijet II Family Overview: The Multijet II family (also known as 1.6 JTDm) includes: - 955A3000 - 1.6L 16V Multijet II, 120 hp, fitted to MiTo (this page) - 955A1000 - 1.3L Multijet, lower‑output diesel - Various 1.6L variants - Different power outputs across Fiat, Alfa Romeo and Abarth models Within the 955A3000, the key specifications are: - Displacement: 1,598 cc - Valves: 16 (4 per cylinder) - Fuel system: Common‑rail diesel - Power: 88 kW (120 PS) - Torque: 320 Nm @ 1,750 rpm - Emissions: Euro 5 (later Euro 6) How to confirm your code: 1. On the engine - the 955A3000 code is stamped on the engine block. Look for "955A3000" or "955 A3.000" on the identification plate. 2. On the V5C logbook - the engine number is listed; cross‑reference with Alfa Romeo parts systems. 3. VIN decode - use an Alfa Romeo VIN decoder; the engine type will be shown. 4. Registration lookup - enter your reg above and we'll confirm the exact fitment. Similar‑looking codes it is commonly confused with: - 955A1000 - 1.4L 8V petrol, fitted to MiTo 1.4 8V - 955A2000 - 1.4L 16V petrol, higher‑output variant - 955A6000 - 1.4L Turbo petrol - 955A8000 - 1.4L MultiAir Turbo petrol Why fitting the wrong revision matters: The 955A3000 is a diesel engine with a completely different fuel system, cylinder head, and ECU compared to the petrol 955 series engines. A petrol 955A1000, 955A2000 or 955A6000 is not a direct swap into a 955A3000‑spec vehicle without significant modifications. Always confirm the exact engine code before ordering a replacement.

relatives.code: Euro 6 1.6 Multijet: The later Euro 6‑compliant version of the 1.6 Multijet II, fitted to post‑2015 MiTo models. It features revised emissions calibration and improved DPF regeneration strategies.

variants.closing: IMPORTANT: The 955A3000 is not the 1.75 TBi petrol engine used in the Giulietta Quadrifoglio Verde. That engine uses a different code.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement 955A3000 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: ** A used 955A3000 makes sense for lower‑value MiTo examples where the car itself is worth under £2,000-£3,000. The key requirement is documented service history showing regular oil changes and evidence that the DPF and EGR have been maintained. The primary risk with used units is undisclosed DPF clogging or EGR issues - insist on a diagnostic scan and DPF pressure test before purchase. Used units typically cost £1,485-£1,800. View used engines

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: ** A proper 955A3000 recon includes DPF professional cleaning or replacement, EGR valve cleaning or replacement, injector refurbishment, turbo inspection, and full gasket set. This is the right call for most replacements - you get a like‑new unit with the known weak points already addressed, backed by 12-24 months warranty. Reconditioned units typically cost £2,182-£2,800. View reconditioned engines

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: ** A full rebuild is justified for low‑mileage, well‑specified or collectable MiTo examples where originality matters. An upgraded rebuild should include new piston rings, bearings, oil pump, turbocharger (if worn), and a full set of gaskets. For standard applications, reconditioned is usually more cost‑effective. View rebuilt engines

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: ** All engines can be supplied and fitted through our network of vetted UK Alfa Romeo specialists - nationwide coverage with 12‑month warranty on labour and parts. View supply & fit
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: ** The 955A3000 sits in the Alfa Romeo MiTo - a supermini with values ranging from £1,500-£5,000 depending on condition and mileage. A £2,182-£2,800 reconditioned engine plus £800-£1,000 fitting is a significant investment - potentially exceeding the vehicle's value. For lower‑value MiTo examples (under £2,500), evaluate the whole‑vehicle condition carefully before committing to a replacement. A used engine with documented DPF and EGR history may be more economic in many cases.

items.question: What are the common problems with the Alfa Romeo 955A3000 engine?
items.answer: The 955A3000's most common issues are EGR valve clogging, DPF blockage (particularly with urban driving), turbocharger wear at higher mileages, and injector wear. The engine is generally reliable when properly maintained but requires regular motorway driving for DPF regeneration. EGR valve cleaning is essential for urban vehicles. DPF regeneration requires regular motorway driving. Regular oil changes with correct specification are critical.
